cinematic.description: Dark, realistic 3D space with slow camera moves, film grain and large serif text. For awe and scale. Pictures here are not to scale; numbers live in the text.

flat.description: Bright flat illustration with bouncy motion and rounded bold text. For playful comparisons.

line.description: Thin lines and dots on black, precise and calm, with light left-aligned text. For orbits, paths and measurements drawn to scale.

light_journey.description: The camera starts at the Sun's surface and flies back with the sunlight past streaking stars until Earth appears as a crescent. Not to scale.

volume_fill.description: Earth pops in, the view zooms out as Jupiter rises at its true size ratio, then Earths are thrown in while Jupiter fills up and a counter runs to the final number.

radius_ratio_fact.description: Jupiter's radius divided by Earth's, used to draw both at their true size ratio

count_fact.description: The number the counter runs up to, e.g. how many Earths fit inside by volume

orbit_clock.description: Planets drawn as dots on circular orbits at their real relative distances, moving at their real relative speeds through one Earth year, each counting its laps.

highlight.description: The planet drawn in the accent colour, with a click on each lap. Must be one of the planets shown.

footnote.description: Small print at the bottom: what is simplified, and the source
